title: Artificial intelligence for higher education: benefits and challenges for pre-service teachers
extended_summary:
This paper examines how pre-service teachers perceive and use artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education, and whether those experiences transfer into their later classroom practice as novice teachers. The study asks whether pre-service teachers are using AI for learning, what benefits and challenges they associate with AI, whether perceptions differ by demographic factors, whether they use AI to support inclusive education, and whether use in study contexts correlates with use in teaching.

The authors conducted an online mixed-methods survey at the University of Latvia. From a larger pool of students, they focused on 240 pre-service teachers who reported on their AI use and perceptions; 147 of these also had teaching experience. The survey combined closed-ended items analyzed with descriptive statistics, Kruskal-Wallis tests, and Spearman correlations, plus open-ended responses analyzed thematically. The context was a single higher education institution in Latvia, where many pre-service teachers are also already working in schools.

Findings show that fewer than half of respondents used AI in their studies, and only about a quarter had used ChatGPT. Students saw clear benefits such as help with language barriers, access to global knowledge, and support for students with disabilities, but they also expressed concerns about laziness, plagiarism, false information, and weaker critical thinking. Although many believed AI could help build more inclusive classrooms, most had not used it in practice. The study found little evidence that AI use during university study translated into AI use in teaching, suggesting a gap between awareness and implementation and a need for stronger AI literacy and practical preparation in teacher education.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed mixed-methods survey study, but it is observational and self-reported rather than experimental. It provides useful descriptive evidence about AI adoption and perceptions, yet it does not establish causal effects on achievement outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests potentially meaningful institutional implications for teacher preparation and AI literacy, but the evidence is based on perceptions and reported use rather than measured achievement gains. There is no direct estimate of effect on middle school mathematics achievement, so impact on the retrieved topic is unclear.

interventions.use_case: Use of ChatGPT and other generative AI tools by pre-service teachers for learning support, information search, language assistance, and classroom-related tasks such as generating questions, lesson ideas, and supporting inclusive teaching.
Use of Google Translate, Grammarly, Microsoft Translator, and Tildes Birojs to handle foreign-language text, grammar correction, and text editing in study work.

finding.finding_summary: The study focuses on pre-service teachers' perceptions of AI/ChatGPT for learning in higher education rather than achievement, but it reports perceived academic benefits such as finding needed information (69% of ChatGPT users, n=54), understanding unfamiliar subjects (61%), and saving time (57%). At the same time, many respondents were ambivalent: 37% reported no AI use, 20% did not know if they had used AI, and 35% thought AI should be banned in the study process.
finding.measure: Self-reported perceived benefits and use of AI tools for learning in higher education
finding.study_size: n=240 (overall survey); n=54 for ChatGPT benefit items

finding.finding_summary: Respondents most commonly used AI tools for language assistance and grammar correction, including translating foreign-language materials and applying Latvian grammar rules. The paper reports that AI helped with language barriers, text understanding, and creating grammatically correct text, but it does not provide achievement effect sizes.
finding.measure: Self-reported use of translation/grammar tools and perceived language-support benefits

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports perceived benefits and risks related to motivation and interest: 66% agreed AI reduces the need to exert oneself and decreases interest in doing research, while 40% were excited about AI's possibilities and many participants were ambivalent or opposed. These are perception data rather than measured learning outcomes, so no effect size is reported.
finding.measure: Self-reported attitudes toward AI-related motivation, laziness, and interest in research

finding.finding_summary: Participants simultaneously endorsed both benefits and risks for critical thinking and problem-solving. Fifty-five percent agreed AI helps develop critical thinking skills and 49% said it helps problem-solving, but 58% also agreed AI-generated information negatively affects these skills and 66% believed it can reduce students' independent reasoning.
finding.measure: Self-reported perceptions of AI's effects on critical thinking and problem-solving

finding.finding_summary: The strongest operational benefit reported was time saving and easier task completion; 57% of ChatGPT users said it helped them save time, and 69% said it helped them find needed information. The paper also notes that respondents saw AI as useful for creating assignments/tests and checking information quality, but it does not test productivity outcomes experimentally.
finding.measure: Self-reported efficiency, time saving, and task-support perceptions
finding.study_size: n=240; n=54 for ChatGPT benefit items

finding.finding_summary: The study argues that AI is underutilized in teacher preparation and that there is a gap between recognizing AI's inclusive potential and actually using it in practice. Among respondents with teaching experience (n=147), 61% agreed AI can include students with different learning needs and 55% agreed it can include students with special needs, but more than half had never used it for those purposes.
finding.measure: Self-reported perceptions and reported classroom use for inclusion and special education
